extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and applicants prosecuting applications before the Japan Patent Office (patent attorneys, in-house counsel, SMEs, universities)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and updated standards for prosecuting patent applications in Japan, covering filing, request for examination, responses to office actions, accelerated procedures, appeals, and divisional strategy. Emphasizes JPO statutory requirements (support/clarity), procedural tips, and eligibility rules for fee reductions and fast-track programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official fee reduction/exemption (SMEs, universities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Official fee reduction/exemption program for SME’s (Small & Medium Enterprises), universities, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No proofs needed. Tip: report the applicant’s status to the local attorney. (Reference: JPO leaflet linked in slides.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination fee calculation and claim-count impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination Fee = basic fee + additional fee/claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple dependent claims, even across different categories, to reduce per-claim additional fees. (Be aware of multi-multi rules — see separate caution.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution on multiple dependent-from-multiple-dependent (multi-multi) claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A multiple dependent claim, dependent from a multiple dependent claim (multi-multi), will not be subjected to a substantive examination (from the application filed on or after April 1, 2022) (Art. 36(6)(iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment to remove multi-multi dependency as a response to an Office Action will lead to a final office action. Avoid filing multi-multi dependencies after the effective date; consider drafting alternatives to multi-multi dependency to save fees without risking prosecution problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer program / software eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: "Computer program" is an eligible product invention, even if it is not stored in a medium (since 2002). "Computer software," "Data structure," etc., are as well (products considered equivalent to a computer program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent eligible inventions categories listed: "Product", "Process" (so-called "simple method"), "Process for producing a product". See JPO guidelines for details on claiming software-related inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation of use (intended use) as a distinguishing factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Intended use/limitation can affect how the examiner treats prior art vs present invention—for example, a crane hook may be recognized as structurally different from a fishing hook if it has appropriate size and strength for crane use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When prior art has a form similar to your invention but different structural suitability for the intended use, emphasize structural/functional differences. Use voluntary amendments or arguments to clarify intended use where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary amendment timing and benefits (use claims / software)
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary amendment can be filed before 1st Office Action. Examination guidelines amended in 2016 for the use claims especially of Foods improved the chances of grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider voluntary amendment of computer software claims or limitations with intended use prior to the first OA to improve grant chances. File timely before first OA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination programs and typical pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: First Action pendency (period from request for examination to first OA) averages: All applications ~10.1 months (as of 2021); PPH / Accelerated Examination ~2.3 months; Super Accelerated Examination ~0.6 months (1.4 months for PCT JP national phase).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PPH/highway pilot and accelerated tracks to drastically shorten first-action pendency when eligible. Links to JPO statistics and programs provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility requirements for Accelerated and Super-Accelerated Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Accelerated examination: Either any one of (1) to (6) is required. Super accelerated examination: All (1) to (3) are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated items (as presented): (1) Already commercialized or to be commercialized within 2 years; (2) A foreign counterpart existing (or 2a/2b variants: 2a foreign counterpart existing, or 2b filed by startups); (3) Applications filed by SMEs, etc.; (4) Green-technology related applications; (5) Earthquake Disaster Recovery Support-related applications; (6) Asian Business Location Law-related applications. Additional practical note: for some eligibility, all filing procedures must have been performed online at least for the most recent 4 weeks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support requirement (Article 36(6)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: "A claimed invention shall be disclosed in the description" (Article 36(6)(i)). The examiner will compare the claimed invention with the invention disclosed in the description to determine whether the support requirement is satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: “Substantial” support for the claimed invention should be found in the description. The object of the invention is considered in the comparison. See JPO guideline references provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of violation of support requirement (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Four types of violation include: (3) Over-broad or over-generalized claims; (4) No recitation of elements necessary for solving the problems discussed in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: (Type 3) Claiming many types of compound R while description only discloses specific examples R1–R3; (Type 4) Claim recites a 'force adjusting unit' but description only discloses a mechanism that increases force as speed increases while the object is to prevent exceeding speed limit. These illustrate why claims may lack substantial support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended responses to support-requirement rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Before amending embodiments, consider arguments that the specification discussion can be generalized to the claimed scope in light of common general knowledge at the filing date; consider submission of experimental results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment to the embodiment might be reasonable in some cases, BUT first attempt explanatory arguments and/or evidence. Use experimental data to support broader claim scope when appropriate. (Tip 4)

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity requirement (Article 36(6)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: "A claimed invention for which a patent is sought shall be clear" (Article 36(6)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms such as "about," "approximately," "substantially," "essentially," "especially," "for example," "etc.," "preferably," and "suitably" would be rejected. Use SI units (m, km, g, kg). Imperial units (inch, feet, yard, pound, ounce) will be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of interviews with JPO examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: JPO examiners are open to: (1) interviews at the JPO building, (2) on-site interviews (examiner travels to applicant's location), and (3) online interviews (Telephone/Web Meeting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews can provide useful hints on how to amend a claim and can be beneficial (on-site useful for showing a product or factory). Consider requesting interviews strategically during prosecution. (Tip 6)

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of examination for divisional applications (when appeal pending)
rubrics_metrics.description: When both an appeal request and divisional application are filed, the examination of the divisional application can be suspended, upon request. Suspension will be maintained until 3 months after the service date of decision of the pre-/appeal, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to decide divisional strategy after conclusion of the appeal. If the divisional becomes unnecessary, withdraw quickly to request a refund of the examination fee. Conditions for suspension: (i) request for examination for the divisional filed on or after April 1, 2023; (ii) examination for the divisional has not yet started; (iii) divisional filed after Decision of Refusal to the parent; (iv) parent is pending to the appeal or pre-appeal; (v) it is convenient to wait for outcome of the appeal. (Tip 7; JPO link provided.)
